input.quote: (ix) it is now and throughout the Term shall comply with all applicable Laws in connection with the operation of its business and the performance of its obligations hereunder or the provision of the Service
input.rationale:
Compliant at or above the preferred position. Vendor (Kubient) gives affirmative express warranties in §9(b) covering every material element of the rule: performance of the Service "in all material respects to industry standards" (p0034); services that "comply with the terms of this Agreement and shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038); no malicious code — "free of any viruses, Trojan Horses, worms, time bombs, trap doors, back doors" (p0036); and compliance with applicable Laws (p0041).

On DURATION (the point flagged by the deterministic check): the warranties are not time-boxed to a short window; they are expressly stated to run "now and throughout the Term" (p0041). The Term is quantified in §4(a) (p0016): "The initial term of this Agreement shall be one (1) year from the Effective Date (the 'Initial Term'). This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms." The warranty duration is therefore a minimum of one (1) year — i.e. twelve (12) months, expressed in years — which satisfies the ≥90-day threshold and meets or exceeds the 12-month (software) / 90-day (services) preferred benchmark. The absence of a stated numeric warranty period is a drafting artifact of a Term-length warranty, not a substantive gap; adding a "ninety (90) days following delivery" period would shorten our protection.

The §13 disclaimer (p0062) does not swallow the express warranties: it applies only "Except as expressly set forth herein" and expressly excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement." The "AS IS with all warranties disclaimed" walk-away scenario is not present.

On REMEDY: there is no repair/replace/refund sentence, but equally no sole- or exclusive-remedy language anywhere in the Agreement (searched: no "sole remedy"). We therefore retain all remedies at law, plus the §4(b) right to terminate for material breach on 30 days' notice if uncured. Inserting the model "at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund" clause would cap our recovery and hand Vendor election of remedy, so per the playbook we do not flag a term that currently benefits our party.

Minor sub-elements noted, not redlined: conformance is measured against "industry standards" and freedom from material errors rather than express conformance to documentation, and there is no separate "professional and workmanlike" formulation. No redline proposed and no counterparty comment required.
